title: Cap. VI Arg. 8: second — efficacious means only from intention of the end; 1 Pet. 1:5
pass_a_gloss: Secondly, that perseverance is not given or destined except to one elected and destined to eternal life is clear from this, that by an agent who understands the force and efficacy of means, means infallibly efficacious for obtaining the end are never prepared and given to anyone except from the purpose and desire of the end. Hither look those words of Peter: by the power of God you are kept through faith unto salvation, 1 Pet. 1:5. God inspires faith into our hearts, keeps what is inspired lest it be extinguished, and therefore does this, that through faith we may be led to salvation. The salvation therefore of all those to whom he decreed to give persevering faith was most certain with God.
pass_b_english: Second: perseverance is given only to one already elected and destined to eternal life. An agent who knows what means can do never prepares and gives infallibly efficacious means except from purpose and desire of the end. So Peter: by God's power you are kept through faith unto salvation (1 Pet. 1:5). God inspires faith, keeps it from going out, and does so that through faith we may be led to salvation. All to whom he decreed persevering faith had salvation most certain with God.
source_text: Secundo, perseverantiam non donari aut destinari nisi ad vitam aeternam electo et destinato, inde clarum est, quod ab agente qui vim et efficaciam mediorum intelligit, media ad finem consequendum infallibiliter efficacia nunquam praeparantur et donantur cuiquam nisi ex proposito et desiderio finis. Huc spectant illa Petri verba, virtute Dei custodimini per fidem ad salutem, 1 Petr. i. 5. Deus inspirat fidem cordibus nostris, inspiratam custodit ne exstinguatur, atque idcirco hoc facit, ut per fidem perducamur ad salutem. Salus igitur eorum omnium fuit apud Deum certissima, quibus fidem perseverantem dare decrevit.
